subject D5 ruled (b-trim/439); S4 review R2 applied; interpretation layer parked
Rulings recorded (S3B_REDESIGN.md §8):
- D5 = b-trim / 439 instances. 368 REJECTED by name: four of the five canonical
  clauses are credited through a patient-free SITUATION atom, so under 368 they
  get no attribution record, price at factor 1.0, and are cap-exempt — m0276 would
  not be suppressed (a §7.2 automatic revert) and m0275/m0466 would restore without
  the `consistent` signature §7.1 binds them to. 746 REJECTED by name: its entire
  marginal reach is two atom names, one an audited false positive whose keyword hit
  is a negation, one a model knowledge-state. 427 recorded as tied-on-measurement.
- Disclosed consequence: the mechanism reaches 79 of 155 target cases, i.e. ~27% of
  the census, not the 53% the class size suggests. BUILD_OVERVIEW.md corrected.

New analysis (all deterministic re-analysis, zero API spend):
- D5_WORKED_EXAMPLES.md — corpus-wide reach measured over every predicted clause
  (panel-blind) with the 155-case census as attention-only cross-check.
- D5B_ACT_ATOMS.md + D5B_COUNTS.md — the act-population question. Ceiling measured
  at ~2 cases, not the ≤17 first assumed; the keyword predicate does not transfer to

- E2_DECISION.md — the S4 gate-off vehicle, and the finding that the F9 version
  convention has outgrown its two hand-written ladders.

S4 (SECTION_PRIOR_DESIGN.md), per S4_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_R2.md:
- E1: the driver does NOT enforce revert on max_regressions; it records PASS/FAIL
  and refuses an unjustified decision. The revert is the DECIDE signer's
  pre-registered obligation. Bound and decision rule unchanged.
- S1: the "4 of 30" census arithmetic was unsound (24/30 intersection; 6 flips

analysed document does not settle are currently recorded as prose in cycle records
and are invisible in tool output. Design parked with triggers; the entry notes the

subject S5 Tier-1 review: REVISE, and the headline is that S5 produces ZERO flips
Measured, not argued: building S5's snapshot (overlay containment.json, frozen
thresholds) and diffing it against join-integrity-v2-2026-08-04 yields no flips on
any of the three behaviours. All 8 clauses that gain subsumption credit were already
predicted; the nearest non-predicted clause misses its cut by 0.043, and forcing
full-credit kind inheritance (2.5x) still yields zero.

So a cycle whose keep/revert 'cites the flip adjudications only' has none to cite,
and it would close KEEP with a clean validator, a passing prediction and zero
adjudications. The gate every widening cycle waits on is unfalsifiable as designed.

Also blocking: S5 is not expressible as a cycle (it changes no file, and the file it
points at is closure-pinned); the expected-effect statement is atom-channel only
while 16 of the 24 changed clauses move through section spillover; and the
patient-composition contract in 5.3 is false under pricing 1.2 (proven on m0355 --
a chained clause atom IS reachable through the overlay once 1.2 dechains it).

Disclosure carried in the review: measuring S5 before OPEN spends its temporal
guarantee. That cannot be restored and must ride into the cycle record.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

author Matt Stults
subject Group 0c: census records the configuration that produced it (S8 prerequisite)
The census tool wrote dossiers with no config identity, so a reader could not tell
which scorer, which join, or which inputs a census reflected. Every other artifact
class here records identity; this one did not.

- config_identity gains mixed_variants; the key is always present.
- generate_dossiers pins join_version for BOTH survey and passage_map -- if they
  disagree the dossiers describe a different join from the one that found the
  disagreements. None keeps the historical v1/uniform default byte-identically.
- benchmark.map_reference threads mixed_variants into inventory.match_passage_v2 and
  records it beside join_version.
- CLI: --join-version {1,2} (default 1, the measured state, always recorded
  explicitly) and --mixed-variants. An impossible pairing raises before minutes of
  loading, and before os.makedirs, so a refusal leaves no half-written directory.

F12 honoured, not 'fixed': join identity stays in CENSUS identity and never enters
snapshot identity. mixed_variants keeps the deliberate False default from 68b036d --
asking for it under --join-version 1 RAISES rather than being silently ignored,
because a silently-ignored flag would make the header's own record false.

The existing 294-case census is left byte-untouched: a header written today would be
a reconstruction asserted as provenance of a run nobody observed. validate refusing
that directory is the correct outcome, and MODULE_MAP §11 records it as an anti-rule
so no future agent retrofits one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 83119967b43987b9431adac976a5d88e2b5dfca5
ordinal 44
date 2026-08-05 17:29:50 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject REVIEW_POLICY amendment: a Tier-2 pass verifying a claim about code must read the code
The two-tier policy's first real use failed in a structural way. The S4 Tier-2 pass
scoped itself to 'design-doc verification only -- no code, no git, no test runs' and
credited two findings FIXED-CORRECT. The next Tier-1 found one did not hold: the
design claimed cycle.py ENFORCES revert on a breached regression bound, and it does
not -- it records a PASS/FAIL check and refuses an unjustified decision, with the
revert being the DECIDE signer's obligation. That claim is entirely about what
cycle.py does, and the pass that verified it never opened cycle.py.

Not carelessness: a design-doc-only reader can confirm a document now SAYS the
right-looking thing, which is what a fix looks like from outside.

Four binding rules added: scope follows the finding not the tier; per-finding
evidence (file and line, or the recomputation) not just a verdict; Tier-2 may not be
the last word before a decision point; purely editorial fixes stay Tier-2, which is
what the tier is genuinely good for.

Also: BUILD_OVERVIEW records the ruled S4-before-S3b order, superseding the earlier
'S3b first, it's 53%' recommendation -- 53% is the class size, not the fix's reach.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

subject affected_parties rename + the attribution seat brief that never existed
RENAME (ruled 2026-08-05): harm_bearers -> affected_parties across the live design
docs -- 55 sites in S3B_REDESIGN, 21 in the task design, 3 in BUILD_OVERVIEW, each
with a naming note at first use so a later reader does not infer two fields. The
mechanism was never harm-only: the procedure's own step 1 asks about 'harm, risk,
protection, or benefit', the population predicate carries benefit keywords, and
m0018 -- 'People should have easy access to trustworthy safety-critical information'
-- is one of the three named restorations and contains no harm at all.

Dated review records keep the old spelling deliberately: they are records of what a
reviewer said on a date, and rewriting them edits the record. The naming notes name
those files explicitly.

BRIEF: briefs/attribution_author.md (264 lines). It did not exist, and HANDOFF wrongly
pointed the attribution seat at backfill_author.md -- the S2 patient-CHAIN brief,
which has zero occurrences of the field and would have run the wrong task.

It carries the fixed 7-step procedure, the pinned noun-phrase table with all its
notes, NEVER INFER verbatim, unclear as a first-class verdict, and two worked
examples verified byte-exact against modelspec_clauses.json: m0018 (a pure benefit
with no harm anywhere -- the case the old field name would have made a seat answer
'unclear' on, failing a control the mechanism handles correctly) and the m0276 trap
('there are people and resources who care' scans third-party, but the atom's risk
falls on the user).

Pricing-silence fence verified independently: zero hits for pricing, discount, taint,
flip, panel, census, golden, revert, snapshot, threshold or any behaviour name. A
seat that knows attributions move scores has a direction to lean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
